question: Select the correct increasing order of atomic radii.
solution:
The correct answer is __**B **__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **B (Boron):** Smallest atomic radius (period 2, group 13).
 
• **Be (Beryllium):** Slightly larger than boron (period 2, group 2).
 
• **Li (Lithium):** Larger than both B and Be (period 2, group 1).
 
• **Rb (Rubidium):** Largest radius (period 5, group 1).n
 
• Thus, the correct increasing order of atomic radii is:
 
 
• **B 
 
 
• **​Atomic radius trend in the periodic table:**
 
• **Across a period (left to right):** Atomic radius decreases due to increased nuclear charge pulling electrons closer.
 
 
• **Down a group (top to bottom):** Atomic radius increases due to the addition of electron shells.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Atomic radius is the distance between an atom's nucleus and its valence electrons.
 
• It is measured in Angstroms(Å).
 
• Atomic radius is used to determine the size of an atom.
 
• When the atomic radius increases, the size of the atom also increases.
